source: IETF notifications whose identity states the transition: RFC 2863 IF-MIB, RFC 4273 BGP4-MIB, RFC 7331 BFD-STD-MIB, RFC 3418 SNMPv2-MIB. Every vendor at once. Title wording and guidance are vendor-neutral (tracker 387, trap semantics); guidance is what such an event usually means, never a diagnosis.

bgp_transition: BGP neighbour {peer}[ (AS {peer_as})][ in VRF {vrf}] on {device} went from {prev_state} to {state}[ ({transition})][ — last error: {last_error}]
BGP neighbour {peer}[ (AS {peer_as})][ in VRF {vrf}] on {device} moved to {state}[ ({transition})][ — last error: {last_error}]
A BGP neighbour on {device} moved to {state}[ ({transition})]

impact: Sustained high CPU can delay control-plane work done in software: routing updates, BFD and tunnel keepalives, management sessions.
Polling and management access to the device may slow down or time out while it lasts.
next_checks: Check whether CPU stays high in the device's own polled CPU metrics, not only in this trap.
List the busiest processes on the device.
Look for control-plane churn at the same time on this device: routing, BFD or tunnel flaps, or a burst of polling.
Check for a recent configuration or software change on the device.

impact: Low free memory can make the device refuse new sessions or routes, or restart processes.
Sustained pressure often precedes a process or device restart.
next_checks: Check the trend of free memory in the device's polled metrics.
List the processes using the most memory on the device.
Check route and session table sizes against the platform's limits.
Check for a recent configuration or software change on the device.

impact: Routes learned from this neighbour are withdrawn: traffic that used them reroutes, or is dropped if there is no other path.
Services reachable only through this neighbour are affected until the session is re-established.
next_checks: Read the last error this event carries (hold timer expired, cease, notification) and the device's BGP log.
Check reachability to the neighbour address and the link toward it.
Check whether BFD, the interface or the tunnel under the session went down at the same time.
Check the neighbour for a reset or configuration change.

impact: This session did not reach Established in the transitions observed, so it carried no routes before or after: this event withdrew nothing.
If the neighbour is expected to be up, the routes or the redundancy it should provide are missing.
next_checks: Confirm the neighbour is configured on the peer side, with matching AS numbers and addresses.
Check TCP port 179 reachability between the session addresses: routing, access lists, firewalls.
Check session authentication and source-address settings on both sides.
If the neighbour is intentionally unused, shut it down or remove it so it stops retrying.

impact: The session is Established again and routes from this neighbour are being relearned.
next_checks: Check how long the session was down and whether it flaps repeatedly.
Confirm the expected prefixes are received again.

impact: A BGP session changed state. Whether routes were affected depends on whether it was Established before, which this event does not show.
next_checks: Check the session's current state and uptime on the device.
Look for the same neighbour's other reports of this transition, which may state the prior state.

impact: Traffic over this interface stops; paths through it reroute if a redundant path exists.
An interface shut down by an operator is down by intent: check the admin status before treating it as a fault.
next_checks: Check the admin status: was the port shut down on purpose?
Check the physical layer: optics, cabling, the far-end port.
Check the interface's error counters before the event.
Check the routing, tunnel or BFD changes that followed.

impact: The path this BFD session watches is considered down; routing or tunnels that rely on it may fail over.
next_checks: Check the underlay path between the two endpoints: loss, latency, interface state.
Check whether other sessions over the same link or transport went down at the same time.
Check for BFD timer or configuration changes on either end.

impact: The device lost a control connection to its controller: policy and route updates may stop reaching it, while forwarding continues on the last state it learned.
next_checks: Check transport reachability from the device to its controllers.
Check the device's certificates and clock synchronisation.
Check whether other devices lost their control connections at the same time, which points at the controller side.

impact: The overlay routing session changed state: routes and TLOCs learned through it may be withdrawn.
next_checks: Check the device's control connections, which the overlay routing session runs over.
Check whether other devices' overlay sessions changed at the same time.
